phases.name: Milestone 1: Reading the shared table
phases.description: Both composition roots (the Netlify entry, with chooseStore, and scripts/serve.mjs) build the restricted port in one change. Reading answers the best ten with listedAt, CDN cache headers and one fixed-reason log line; failures answer 500 without leaking player details.

steps.name: Restricted port wired through both roots; empty table read
criteria: A GET of an empty table answers 200 with no rows and a listedAt, cached 15 s at the CDN, logged scores.read ok with scope local.
The walking skeleton stays green in all three browsers, with scripts/serve.mjs signing and reading through createTablePort and passing the function's own headers through.
(unit) chooseStore returns 'site' only for context 'production' with published true: all 12 ADR-005 cases pass, and no other context reaches the site store.
Over a fake deploy environment the Netlify entry answers and logs scope deploy with the raw context and published; without a deploy ID it answers 500 unexpected (store-unavailable).
The exported config is exactly path /api/scores and rateLimit 10 per 60 s by ip and domain; a GET handed only list still answers 200.
No __SCAFFOLD__ throw remains in scores.mjs for createTablePort, chooseStore, encodeKey, decodeKey or rankKeys.
steps.scenario_name: An empty high-score table is read as empty, and everyone sees it at most 15 seconds old
steps.implementation_notes: The inseparable change (DISTILL, WS strategy): handleScores(request, port, options) replaces handleScores(req, store), and the Netlify default export and scripts/serve.mjs build the port in the same change, or the walking skeleton and the production entry break. createTablePort(store) -> { list, putIfNew, remove } (DDD-4): list() = the keys under s/ matching ^s/\d{7}-\d{15}-[A-Z]{3}-[a-z0-9]+$, in arcade order; putIfNew(key) = store.set(key, '', { onlyIfNew: true }), true if written; remove(key) = store.delete(key); putIfNew and remove throw a refusal (a distinguishable error) for any key that isn't well-formed; no other store method. Call only store.list, store.set and store.delete: the harness's test store port (steps/table-service.js, a second composition root) intercepts exactly those. GET is handed list alone. options = { now, newId, log, where }: now stands in for Date.now (the key's time, and listedAt = now() right after list returns); newId for the id; log receives one entry per request { event, reason, ms, keys?, scope, context, published }, where = { scope, context, published } logged as given, and all three 'missing' if a root omits it. GET 200 = { scores: at most 10 { initials, score, id }, best first, listedAt }, with Netlify-CDN-Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=15, durable and Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate; every other answer Cache-Control: no-store; every answer Content-Type application/json, Netlify-Vary: query=table and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff (DDD-6). Log scores.read ok with keys = the well-formed keys listed. Pure helpers, exported: encodeKey({ initials, score, at, id }) -> s/{9999999 - score, 7 digits}-{at, 15 digits}-{initials}-{id}; decodeKey(key) -> the row or null; rankKeys(keys) -> the well-formed keys in arcade order; chooseStore(context) -> 'site' only when context?.deploy?.context === 'production' and context?.deploy?.published === true, else 'deploy' (ADR-005). Until 02-01 the POST keeps the skeleton's validation, and until 03-01 its fixed prune, both moved onto the port; it answers { scores, id, listedAt }. Take TABLE_SIZE and MAX_SCORE from ../../src/game/high-scores.js, the one import from src/ that netlify/ may make. Entry: default export (req, context): kind = chooseStore(context); getStore({ name: 'leaderboard', consistency: 'strong' }) for 'site', getDeployStore({ name: 'leaderboard', consistency: 'strong' }) for 'deploy'; where = { scope: kind, context: context?.deploy?.context ?? 'missing', published: context?.deploy?.published ?? 'missing' } (raw values); now = Date.now; newId = randomUUID() without hyphens (it must match [a-z0-9]+); log = one JSON line on console. If opening the store throws (MissingBlobsEnvironmentError without a deploy ID), answer 500 { error: 'unexpected' } with the no-store headers, logged scores.error store-unavailable; never fall back to the site store. config = { path: '/api/scores', rateLimit: { windowLimit: 10, windowSize: 60, aggregateBy: ['ip', 'domain'] } } (DEVOPS pre-requisite 2). scripts/serve.mjs: per request, createTablePort over the cookie's store (leaderboard-<board>, else leaderboard-local) and handleScores(request, port, { now: Date.now, newId, log, where: { scope: 'local', context: 'missing', published: 'missing' } }); stop forcing cache-control: no-store on /api/scores and pass the function's headers through (DEVOPS pre-requisite 5). Unit tests: tests/unit/choose-store.spec.js (the 12 ADR-005 cases as a `// bypass:` table, plus a property that every other context gives 'deploy'); tests/unit/score-keys.spec.js (encode/decode round trip and rankKeys order as properties; decodeKey gives null for malformed keys, the emulator's s/.xxxx included); tests/unit/scores-entry.spec.js (the default export over a fake deploy environment on a real BlobsServer: NETLIFY_BLOBS_CONTEXT with edgeURL, uncachedEdgeURL, siteID, token and deployID, restored afterwards; it answers and logs scope deploy, context deploy-preview, published false; production with published true logs scope site; with no deployID, 500 unexpected logged store-unavailable; and the exported config contract, config only, because the per-answer headers are the @server scenarios'); tests/unit/scores-handler.spec.js (a GET handed { list } alone answers 200). With this step ADR-005 is implemented; pushing the branch still needs the user's OK. TEST PARADIGM: new unit tests go in tests/unit (the unit project: Node only, no browser, as on Netlify's build image), import ./support/seed.js so FC_SEED replays a failure, and are fast-check properties, with assertStateDelta (tests/common/state-delta.js) over a declared universe wherever a call changes state; a single example needs a `// bypass:` reason. Acceptance scenarios are DISTILL's: run each with RUN_PENDING=1 first, then enable it by deleting its @pending, one at a time; never edit steps, drivers or harnesses. Done when this step's scenarios are green and PORT=4174 CI=1 npm test and PORT=4174 CI=1 npm run build stay green.

steps.name: Ranked reads, ignored strays, failures that leak nothing
criteria: A GET answers the best ten well-formed rows, best first, the earlier of equal deposits first; stray keys are neither shown nor removed.
A listing that throws answers 500 unexpected, no-store, logged scores.error list-failed, and nothing logged names a key, initials or an id.
handleScores always resolves: any unexpected throw answers 500 unexpected, logged scores.error unexpected, and no console method ever receives a key or initials.
scripts/serve.mjs logs only a fixed reason and deletes its emulator directory on exit, SIGINT and SIGTERM; a test shows the directory gone.
The import scan enforces the five layering rules over src and netlify, and recognises all four import forms, including dynamic import().
steps.scenario_name: The table shows the best ten signatures, best first, and the earlier of two equal deposits first | Stray entries that aren't signatures are ignored when the table is read | A reader is told the table failed when it can't be looked at, and the owner is told why, without the player's details
steps.implementation_notes: Nothing escapes the handler (DDD-17, DEVOPS pre-requisite 4): a catch-all around the request handling turns any throw into 500 { error: 'unexpected' }, no-store, logged once as scores.error unexpected, so handleScores never rejects; known failures keep their own reason (a GET whose listing throws: 500 unexpected, logged list-failed). Never log an error's message, a key, the body, an id, initials or an IP. M1's ranking and stray-entry scenarios should pass on enablement after 01-01 (the keys sort as strings into arcade order; the port lists well-formed keys only): confirm, then un-pend. tests/unit/scores-log-leak.spec.js: the real port over a real BlobsServer store whose list, set and delete throw an Error carrying a score key (for example s/9999000-001767225600000-FAB-t1), handled with the production console logger (export it from scores.mjs, or go through the entry over a fake environment); capture console.log, info, warn, error, debug and trace, and assert that none receives s/\d{7}-, the initials or the id; also make now() throw, and assert 500 unexpected and the same silence. scripts/serve.mjs (DEVOPS pre-requisite 5, DDD-16): its own catch logs a fixed line only (scores.error, unexpected, scope local), never console.error(error); it stops the emulator and deletes its temp directory on exit, SIGINT and SIGTERM (a synchronous rm on 'exit'); no start-up sweep, which could delete a side-by-side checkout's live directory. tests/unit/serve-cleanup.spec.js: spawn node scripts/serve.mjs with a spare PORT and its own TMPDIR (os.tmpdir() honours it), wait until it serves, send SIGTERM (and SIGINT in a second run), and assert that its make-the-right-move-blobs-* directory is gone (`// bypass:` a process lifecycle, not a property). Playwright's webServer, per its docs, SIGKILLs the server when gracefulShutdown is unset, so the cleanup would never run after npm test or npm run build: set webServer.gracefulShutdown to { signal: 'SIGTERM', timeout: 2000 } in playwright.config.js, its only change, and flag it to the orchestrator (DISTILL left the config alone). tests/unit/layering.spec.js: a hand-rolled import scan over src/** and netlify/** that matches import ... from '...', bare import '...', export ... from '...' and dynamic import('...'), and checks the five rules (ADR-006): game/ imports only from game/ and theme/; theme/ imports nothing; game/high-scores.js imports nothing; src/** never imports netlify/** or @netlify/*; netlify/** imports only src/game/high-scores.js from src/. Check the scanner itself on inline sources for each import form. No new devDependency. TEST PARADIGM: new unit tests go in tests/unit (the unit project: Node only, no browser, as on Netlify's build image), import ./support/seed.js so FC_SEED replays a failure, and are fast-check properties, with assertStateDelta (tests/common/state-delta.js) over a declared universe wherever a call changes state; a single example needs a `// bypass:` reason. Acceptance scenarios are DISTILL's: run each with RUN_PENDING=1 first, then enable it by deleting its @pending, one at a time; never edit steps, drivers or harnesses. Done when this step's scenarios are green and PORT=4174 CI=1 npm test and PORT=4174 CI=1 npm run build stay green.

phases.name: Milestone 2: Signing the shared table
phases.description: Every valid signature becomes a row of its own; anything else is refused and saves nothing: 415, 413 (a 1,024-byte cap), 400 for shape or the word filter, 405, 503 for an existing key, 500 for store failures and port refusals. Split for @sizing-review-needed.

steps.name: Save valid signatures; refuse wrong format, size or shape
criteria: A valid POST adds exactly one well-formed key and answers 200 with scores, id and a listedAt taken after its post-write listing, no-store.
Signing the same initials and deposit twice makes two rows; £50, £9,999,950 and a body padded to exactly 1,024 bytes are accepted.
A non-JSON content type answers 415 json-required; a body over 1,024 bytes answers 413 payload-too-large, even when Content-Length claims 20.
Bad JSON, extra or missing fields, lowercase initials, or a score that isn't a positive £50 multiple up to £9,999,999 answer 400 invalid-signature.
Every refusal saves nothing, answers no-store JSON with its error, and logs scores.rejected with that reason; a signing logs scores.signed ok with keys.
steps.scenario_name: A valid signature is saved, and the answer shows where it ranks | Signing twice with the same initials and deposit makes two rows | The table accepts the signature <signature> | The table refuses <what> <why>, and saves nothing
steps.implementation_notes: First half of M2 (@sizing-review-needed, 10 scenarios: split into 02-01 and 02-02, 4 + 6 scenarios). POST checks, in this order (ADR-007): the media type must be application/json (parameters ignored), else 415 json-required; the body is read from the stream with a cap of 1,024 bytes, stopping at the 1,025th, Content-Length never trusted, else 413 payload-too-large; then JSON.parse and isValidSignature, else 400 invalid-signature. Implement isValidSignature in src/game/high-scores.js: shape only, exactly the two fields { initials, score }, three letters of ALPHABET, a safe integer above 0, a multiple of SCORE_STEP, at most MAX_SCORE; the word filter is a separate question (02-02). The server takes SCORE_STEP from there and drops the skeleton's own constants and isValid. A valid signature: putIfNew(encodeKey({ initials, score, at: now(), id: newId() })), then list; answer 200 { scores, id, listedAt } from that listing, listedAt = now() right after it returns, no-store; log scores.signed ok with keys = the well-formed keys in that listing. Refusals answer { error } with no-store and log scores.rejected with the error code as the reason, plus ms and where. The browser already sends application/json, so the walking skeleton stays green. Unit test in tests/unit/scores-handler.spec.js: a POST declaring Content-Length: 20 with a 1,025-byte body answers 413 and saves nothing (moved out of M2 by DISTILL to keep the Gherkin in business language). TEST PARADIGM: new unit tests go in tests/unit (the unit project: Node only, no browser, as on Netlify's build image), import ./support/seed.js so FC_SEED replays a failure, and are fast-check properties, with assertStateDelta (tests/common/state-delta.js) over a declared universe wherever a call changes state; a single example needs a `// bypass:` reason. Acceptance scenarios are DISTILL's: run each with RUN_PENDING=1 first, then enable it by deleting its @pending, one at a time; never edit steps, drivers or harnesses. Done when this step's scenarios are green and PORT=4174 CI=1 npm test and PORT=4174 CI=1 npm run build stay green.

steps.name: Word filter, method refusals, duplicate rows and store failures
criteria: A POST with any of the 16 owner-reviewed initials (ASS, COK, CUM, DIK, FAG, FCK, FUC, FUK, KKK, NAZ, NGR, NIG, PIS, SEX, SHT, TIT) answers 400 initials-not-allowed and saves nothing.
DELETE or PUT answers 405 method-not-allowed with Allow: GET, POST and no-store, logged scores.rejected method-not-allowed; the table is unchanged.
A signature whose key already exists answers 503 not-saved, logged scores.not_saved key-exists, and no second row is written.
A failed write answers 500 unexpected, logged put-failed, adding at most one row; a listing failing after the write answers 500 unexpected, logged list-failed, keeping the row.
A key the port refuses answers 500 unexpected, logged unexpected, and writes nothing; no log line names the player.
steps.scenario_name: Initials on the word filter are refused by the table too | Asking the table to <demand> is refused, because it can only be read or signed | A signature that would land on an existing row is turned away, not saved twice | A signature the table fails to save is reported as an unexpected failure | A signature saved just before the table can't be looked at stays saved, though the signer isn't told | A new row the table can't file is refused, and nothing is written
steps.implementation_notes: Second half of M2. Precondition 0, resolved by the user: BLOCKED_INITIALS in src/game/high-scores.js becomes Object.freeze(['ASS', 'COK', 'CUM', 'DIK', 'FAG', 'FCK', 'FUC', 'FUK', 'KKK', 'NAZ', 'NGR', 'NIG', 'PIS', 'SEX', 'SHT', 'TIT']), exactly these 16. The acceptance tests take BLOCKED_INITIALS[0] as their example, so their DATA GAP closes here (M2 now; M5 and M8 later). isAllowedInitials(initials): three letters of ALPHABET and not in BLOCKED_INITIALS. Handler: after a valid shape, blocked initials answer 400 initials-not-allowed, logged scores.rejected initials-not-allowed. Any method but GET and POST, checked first: 405 { error: 'method-not-allowed' }, Allow: GET, POST, no-store, logged scores.rejected method-not-allowed. putIfNew false: 503 { error: 'not-saved' }, logged scores.not_saved key-exists. putIfNew throws: 500 unexpected, logged scores.error put-failed. The listing after the write throws: 500 unexpected, logged list-failed (the row stays; the client will show unconfirmed, ADR-008). A port refusal: 500 unexpected, logged unexpected. Don't validate or clean the id before the port: refusing a key is the port's job, and the harness forces an id outside [a-z0-9]+ to prove it. phases.name: Milestone 3: No signature is lost
phases.description: Each signing tidies away min(5, n - 20) scores ranked 11th or lower, best effort, never a stray entry. A burst of up to 30 loses nothing locally; the preview smoke script, behind its write guard, carries the same check to real Netlify (K10-K14).

steps.name: Bounded best-effort pruning of old scores below the top ten
criteria: After a save, exactly min(5, n - 20) keys ranked 11th or lower are removed, n being the well-formed keys listed after the write; none up to 20.
With 19, 20 and 30 scores held, a signing tidies away 0, 1 and 5 old scores, and every stray entry survives.
When every removal fails, the signing still answers 200 with its row at #1, removes no score, and logs scores.signed prune-failed without player details.
A port refusal while pruning answers 500 unexpected, never 200 with prune-failed.
(unit) planPrune, as a property over any ranked listing, returns min(5, n - 20) keys, all ranked 11th or lower, and none for 20 keys or fewer; its __SCAFFOLD__ throw is gone.
steps.scenario_name: With <held> scores already kept, a new signing tidies away <loses> | A signing is still saved and answered when tidying up fails
steps.implementation_notes: DDD-1, exact rule accepted by the user (2026-10-24): planPrune(ranked) returns k = min(5, n - 20) keys when n, the number of well-formed keys in the listing taken after the write, is above 20, and none otherwise. Every key it returns is ranked 11th or lower (from ranked.slice(10)); which of those is the crafter's choice, and it may be the new key itself (accepted: that signing's answer then shows it off the table, ADR-008). This replaces the skeleton's fixed delete-5 in prune(). After the post-write listing, remove each planned key through port.remove. Best effort: a store failure while removing is caught, the answer is still 200 with the top 10 of that listing (pruning never touches it), and the request's one log line is scores.signed prune-failed. A port refusal is a bug, never prune-failed: 500 unexpected, logged unexpected (DDD-4). keys in the log = the well-formed keys in the post-write listing. Unit tests: in tests/unit/score-keys.spec.js, a planPrune property over ranked listings of 0 to 40 keys; in tests/unit/scores-handler.spec.js, a refusal during pruning (the real port, with remove passing on a key it refuses) answers 500 unexpected and never prune-failed. steps.name: No signature lost under a burst; preview smoke script
criteria: Any batch of up to 30 simultaneous valid signatures gets 200 for each, and the table read afterwards is exactly their best 10.
scripts/smoke-leaderboard.mjs implements the four DEVOPS modes, prints one JSON summary, and exits 1 on a failed hard check and 2 on a guard refusal.
The write guard refuses any POST to the custom domain, <site>.netlify.app, main--<site>, a permalink outside the unpublished check, or any other non-preview host.
The unpublished check refuses when the published deploy's ID equals the permalink's or can't be learned; no POST precedes a first GET answering 200 with no rows.
.netlify/ is ignored by git, and nothing is pushed, deployed or run against Netlify in this step.
steps.scenario_name: However many signatures arrive at once, none that belongs in the top ten is lost
steps.implementation_notes: Enable M3's @property (OUT-9, the local twin of K11). It should pass on enablement: one key per score loses nothing (SPIKE). It runs 20 batches of up to 30 on the real emulator with seed 20261023, and a failure replays with FC_SEED. It checks that every signer gets 200 and that the table read afterwards is the true top 10, not that each signer finds its own row: the emulator can cut a listing short under concurrent writes, so that is K11's check, on Netlify. scripts/smoke-leaderboard.mjs follows the DEVOPS spec 'Preview smoke test' in feature-delta.md: Node 22 fetch, no dependencies; it imports src/game/high-scores.js for valid and blocked initials. Modes: --site --preview [--production] [--permalink] (steps 1 and 4-10); --site --burst (steps 1-3); --production alone (GET only, P1-P3); --site --unpublished --production, with NETLIFY_AUTH_TOKEN and --site-id, or interactive (U1-U3). Every step stays under 10 requests per 60 s per host, except steps 2, 8a, 8b and 9, each followed by a 61 s wait; an inconclusive step is never a pass; it prints the full response headers of step 1, step 4 and the first POST of step 6; one JSON summary; exit 1 on a failed hard check, 2 on a guard refusal. Write guard, checked before every POST in every mode: (1) POST only to deploy-preview-<n>--<site>.netlify.app or <branch>--<site>.netlify.app, <site> taken from --site; refuse the custom domain, <site>.netlify.app, main--<site>.netlify.app, any host whose prefix is a 24-character deploy ID, and any other host; (2) only the unpublished check may POST to a permalink, and only if its ID differs from the published deploy's, learned from published_deploy.id in GET https://api.netlify.com/api/v1/sites/<site ID> (confirm the field name in Netlify's API reference first) or typed back by the owner as a 24-character ID different from the target's, never from a command-line flag; a failed or empty answer refuses; (3) the run's first request to the host is a GET, and a POST is allowed only after it answered 200 with scores: []. phases.name: Milestone 4: Only a deposit that makes the table is asked
phases.description: The browser's table state, ordered by listedAt, and makesTheTable from the shared rules decide who is asked for initials. The rules gain snapshot(), main.js hands answers over between frames, and the page gains the initials field.

steps.name: Ask for initials only when the deposit makes the table
criteria: With 9 rows of £1,000, a £50 deposit is asked for initials, and the initials field reads 'A A A, letter 1 of 3'.
makesTheTable is true only for an available table and a deposit above 0, with fewer than 10 rows or above the 10th; a tie misses.
Through snapshot(): load rows apply only when listedAt is at least the last applied; a failed first load makes the table unavailable, later failures change nothing.

Every hurdle value and Dream Home bonus is a multiple of SCORE_STEP from src/game/high-scores.js, which no longer carries __SCAFFOLD__ (marker and helper gone); game.js has no scaffold throw left for tableAnswered, tableFailed or snapshot.
The guards stay green: the walking skeleton, both M4 guards, M6's title scenario, and M5's sent-once and Enter outlines.
steps.scenario_name: A deposit is asked for initials while the table has room
steps.implementation_notes: src/game/high-scores.js: makesTheTable(table, deposit) is true only when table.status is 'available', the deposit is above 0, and there are fewer than TABLE_SIZE rows or the deposit beats the last row's score (a tie misses); then delete export const __SCAFFOLD__ (nothing imports it). src/game/game.js: g.table { status: 'unknown' | 'available' | 'unavailable', rows } replaces g.highScores, plus the last applied listedAt; the table constants come from ./high-scores.js; game over opens the entry (A A A, the first letter current) only if makesTheTable(g.table, g.score). tableAnswered({ scores, listedAt }) applies the rows only if listedAt >= the last applied (rows replaced, status available, last applied = listedAt), and ignores them otherwise (DDD-12). tableFailed(): unknown becomes unavailable; any other status stays (DDD-9). snapshot(): a fresh, frozen { screen: 'title' | 'play' | 'over' ('dead' and 'clear' are 'play'), table: { status, rows } (rows [] while unknown), entry: { letters as a string such as 'AAA', index } or null, signing, settled, lastListedAt (null before any) }; Tier B reads the rules only through it. src/main.js: the page-load leaderboard.load() hands its whole answer { scores, listedAt } to tableAnswered, or calls tableFailed, from the promise callbacks, between frames (DDD-11); src/platform/leaderboard.js's load resolves the whole answer. Unit tests in tests/unit/high-scores.spec.js: a makesTheTable property beyond what M4 and M8 cover (status, a deposit of 0, ties, a full table); and every HURDLES value and DREAM_BONUSES entry in src/theme/theme.js is a multiple of SCORE_STEP (DESIGN, Reuse Analysis). phases.name: Milestone 5: Every signing has an outcome
phases.description: A signing is pending until its answer, then confirmed (rank and marked row), off the table, or unconfirmed (not OK, network error, or the 5000 ms timeout). Initials entry is announced letter by letter, and blocked initials are refused in the game. Split for @sizing-review-needed.

steps.name: Pending, confirmed, off-table and unconfirmed, with the 5 s timeout
criteria: Signing FAB shows 'Signing FAB…' until the table answers, with no row marked; the skeleton's optimistic 'Signed FAB.' is gone.
An answer with the new id says 'Signed FAB, #1.' and marks that row aria-current; without it, 'The table filled up before FAB arrived.'
A dropped connection, a 503, or no answer within exactly 5000 ms says 'Couldn't confirm FAB's signing.'; at 4.9 s it still says 'Signing FAB…'.
Each settled outcome, a replaced signing's included, is announced exactly once by the status mirror; a signing is sent once and never retried.
